name: Siamese bi-temporal change detection, with weak temporal supervision

identity.method_name: Siamese bi-temporal change detection network (FC-Siam-diff/conc, ChangeFormer-style, or Changen2's ChangeStar decoder), pretrained or synthetically supervised via weak-temporal-supervision pseudo-pairs (arXiv 2601.02126) and/or Changen2 generative change foundation model (arXiv 2406.17998)
identity.core_idea: A Siamese (shared-weight, two-branch) CNN or transformer encodes the 2019 and 2025 scene patches separately, then a decoder compares the two feature maps (difference or concatenation) to output a per-pixel change mask. Because no labelled 2019-to-2025 change mask exists for these lakes, two 2024-2026 approaches try to supply supervision without real bi-temporal labels: (1) weak temporal supervision (arXiv 2601.02126) synthesises 'fake' change pairs by cross-pairing single-date images from different locations and scoring object-level semantic IoU between their masks, mixed with real same-location pairs assumed unchanged; (2) Changen2 (arXiv 2406.17998) trains a resolution-scalable diffusion transformer as a generative probabilistic change model that can synthesise whole bi-temporal image + change-label series from a single unlabelled image, giving a model with claimed zero-shot change-detection ability out of the box.
identity.official_dataset_ids: None of the project's own Sentinel-2/OSM assets apply here as an 'official ID' for this method; the method's own reference benchmarks are LEVIR-CD (justchenhao.github.io/LEVIR), WHU-CD (DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2018.2858817), and S2Looking (DOI 10.3390/rs13245094) -- reproduced exactly as their own paper/dataset names, none of which are Earth Engine or STAC catalogue IDs.

fit_to_project.ground_truth_proxy_strategy: Combination of 'transfer from another labelled dataset' (LEVIR-CD/WHU-CD/S2Looking pretrained checkpoints, used zero-shot or fine-tuned) and 'zero-shot foundation model' (Changen2's generative pretraining) and 'programmatic weak supervision' (the 2601.02126 pseudo-pair trick, which could in principle be re-run using the project's own MNDWI/NDVI single-date masks as the semantic input instead of FLAIR/IAILD land-cover masks). None of the three supplies a real 'encroached vs not' label for these lakes -- they only supply a generic 'pixel/object changed' signal that a student must still map onto 'encroachment' by a separate, manual rule. Cost: building a working weak-temporal-supervision pipeline from the project's own MNDWI/NDVI masks is a non-trivial reimplementation (the paper's code was 'to be released' as of its Jan 2026 submission and had not been confirmed public as of this research), realistically several student-days beyond just calling a pretrained checkpoint.
fit_to_project.input_required: Two co-registered multi-band scenes per lake (2019, 2025), which the project already has cached (B02,B03,B04,B08,B11,SCL at 20 m). Also needs, for the weak-temporal route, single-date semantic masks to build pseudo-pairs (the project's own MNDWI/NDVI thresholds could serve, at the cost of circularity -- see leakage_risk) and, for any checkpoint reuse, a resolution/normalisation adaptation layer since none of the reference checkpoints were trained at 20 m.
fit_to_project.viable_with_42_rows: only-if-reframed. The method operates per-pixel or per-patch within a single 2019-vs-2025 pair per lake, not per lake-year, so the 42-row lake-year table is irrelevant here. The effective sample for training/adaptation is 6 image pairs (one per lake), or, if tiled into small patches, on the order of a few hundred patches per lake -- but those patches are drawn from the same water body and the same two dates, so they are heavily spatially autocorrelated pseudo-samples, not 6 x N independent observations. The real effective sample size for any held-out evaluation is 6 lakes.
fit_to_project.viable_without_ground_truth: needs-weak-labels. Both 2601.02126 and Changen2 remove the need for a real labelled change mask by generating pseudo/synthetic supervision, but neither removes the need for a definition of 'encroachment' -- a generic spectral or building change mask must still be filtered/interpreted by the student against MNDWI/NDVI/OSM to decide which detected changes are encroachment versus desilting, hyacinth growth, or seasonal variation.
fit_to_project.resolution_match_20m: This is the central, unresolved problem for this item. LEVIR-CD is 0.5 m/px (justchenhao.github.io/LEVIR), WHU-CD is ~0.2 m/px (DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2018.2858817), and S2Looking -- despite the 'S2' in its name, which invites confusion with Sentinel-2 -- is 0.5-0.8 m/px VHR imagery from GaoFen/SuperView/BeiJing-2 satellites (DOI 10.3390/rs13245094), not Sentinel-2 at all. Both the weak-temporal-supervision paper (tested only on 0.2-1.5 m/px aerial/SPOT imagery: BD ORTHO, FLAIR, IAILD, SPOT-6/7) and Changen2 (trained on xView2 and OpenEarthMap, both sub-2 m VHR) report zero evaluation on Sentinel-2 or any 10-20 m imagery [verify -- confirmed absent from both primary-source abstracts/bodies retrieved]. At 20 m, an individual building (the object class these checkpoints were built to detect) is far below one pixel, so a checkpoint trained to spot 5-40-pixel-wide buildings has no equivalent visual pattern to lock onto at 20 m; the resolution gap the project's own note warns about is real and neither 2026 paper closes it.
fit_to_project.label_source_needed: None for using a pretrained checkpoint zero-shot; the project's own MNDWI/NDVI thresholded masks if attempting to reproduce the weak-temporal-supervision pseudo-pair recipe in-house.
fit_to_project.fixes_which_stated_limitation: Partially addresses (4), the dry-season-minimum-only limitation, only in the narrow sense that it forces an explicit 2019-vs-2025 comparison rather than a single snapshot -- but it does not add more scenes per year. It does not fix (1) the 42-row limit, (2) the single-snapshot OpenStreetMap building layer, or (3) the absence of ground truth (it substitutes synthetic supervision, not verified ground truth, for the missing labels).
fit_to_project.handles_desilting_confound: No. A generic Siamese/diffusion change detector flags any large spectral or structural difference between 2019 and 2025 as 'change' -- it has no built-in concept of 'lake drained for maintenance versus lake permanently filled by encroachment.' Bellandur's 15.7 ha (2019) to 0.4 ha (2021) to 107.9 ha (2025) trajectory would register as a large change signal indistinguishable from encroachment without an external cross-check (DEM/bathymetry, item D7, or official desilting records).
fit_to_project.handles_hyacinth_confound: No, not inherently. The pretrained taxonomies behind LEVIR-CD/WHU-CD/S2Looking are building-centric and contain no macrophyte/hyacinth class; the weak-temporal-supervision pipeline's pseudo-labels come from off-the-shelf land-cover segmentation models (FLAIR/IAILD classes) that are also not tuned for floating vegetation mats. Any change map for Bellandur or Varthur would need to be cross-checked against the published macrophyte-cover mapping (MDPI Remote Sensing 2020, DOI 10.3390/rs12223843) to separate a hyacinth bloom/die-off from a genuine land-cover change.
fit_to_project.legal_traceability: Output change pixels map only to whichever OpenStreetMap-derived buffer polygon they are intersected with after the fact (30 m Supreme-Court-reinstated Bengaluru Master Plan buffer, or the quashed 75 m NGT buffer, per item B1) -- the change-detection model itself carries no cadastral or legal reference. Testing the 30 m buffer at 20 m pixel resolution means the buffer is only 1.5 pixels wide, so any change map is far too coarse to make a buffer-specific legal claim; it can only support a qualitative, lake-wide statement.
fit_to_project.temporal_granularity: The method as specified compares exactly two dates (2019, 2025); it does not use the intervening 5 years of the project's own annual Sentinel-2 archive at all, so it throws away most of the temporal signal the project has already collected. Any single 'change since 2019' map is a snapshot difference, not a trend, and cannot distinguish a monotonic decline from a drain-then-refill step change (that needs item C9's break-detection instead).

implementation.libraries: PyTorch (>=2.0); Open-CD toolbox (github.com/likyoo/open-cd) or Z-Zheng/pytorch-change-models for Changen2/ChangeStar; the weak-temporal-supervision authors' own repo at the project page (code state unconfirmed, see pretrained_weights); torchgeo optional for Sentinel-2 I/O.
implementation.pretrained_weights: Changen2 checkpoints and training code are published at github.com/Z-Zheng/pytorch-change-models (built on top of the ICCV 2023 Changen predecessor, github.com/Z-Zheng/Changen), trained on xView2 (pre/post-disaster VHR) and OpenEarthMap (global VHR land cover), both sub-2 m. For arXiv 2601.02126, the paper (submitted 5 Jan 2026) states code and datasets 'will be released publicly' via the project page https://xavibou.github.io/CDviaWTS/; as of this research (Sept 2026) public availability of that code was not independently confirmed and should be re-checked before committing student time to it. [uncertain]
implementation.licence: Changen2 / pytorch-change-models: Apache 2.0 on GitHub, usable in an academic project. Weak-temporal-supervision (2601.02126) code licence: unknown/not yet published [uncertain]. LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD and S2Looking are released for research use, which is fine for an academic capstone, but none of their licences matter if the resolution gap makes the checkpoints unusable here.
implementation.compute_requirement: Using either model zero-shot (frozen inference) is CPU-feasible or fits comfortably on a free Colab/Kaggle GPU (T4-class) in minutes per lake pair. Fine-tuning Changen2's diffusion transformer, or re-implementing the pseudo-pair training recipe from scratch on the project's own masks, is realistically outside laptop-CPU territory and would consume a meaningful share of free-tier GPU quota; this is also explicitly out of scope per the project's own decision to use foundation models frozen rather than fully fine-tuned (see item A6).
implementation.student_days: 3-5 days to run either checkpoint zero-shot on the 6 lake pairs and document that it does not produce a usable encroachment signal at 20 m (a legitimate null-result deliverable). 10-15 days if attempting a genuine adaptation (re-implementing the weak-temporal-supervision pseudo-pair recipe using the project's own MNDWI/NDVI masks, or fine-tuning a small decoder on top of frozen Changen2/backbone features), with no guarantee of a usable result at the end.

evaluation.metrics: Change-class F1 and IoU against the project's own MNDWI/NDVI-difference proxy mask (not a real ground truth), reported alongside a qualitative overlay against known desilting-year and hyacinth-year evidence. Accuracy alone would be meaningless since 'no change' pixels dominate every lake buffer by a wide margin.
evaluation.validation_protocol: leave-one-lake-out is the only defensible option if any training/fine-tuning is attempted (6 folds, one lake held out each time); for purely zero-shot use of a frozen checkpoint there is no train/test split to leak, but any threshold tuned by looking at the 6 lakes' own results before reporting them is itself a form of leakage and must be disclosed as such.
evaluation.leakage_risk: With only 6 lakes and one 2019-vs-2025 pair each, patches drawn from the same lake are strongly spatially autocorrelated (same water body, same imaging conditions, same shoreline geometry), so any patch-level random split leaks lake identity into both train and test and will overstate performance. If the weak-temporal pseudo-pair recipe is rebuilt using the project's own MNDWI/NDVI masks as the semantic input, the resulting 'change' labels are definitionally derived from the same rule the deep model is meant to be judged against, so any apparent agreement is circular, not independent validation.
evaluation.uncertainty_reporting: None by default from either the pretrained checkpoints or a from-scratch pseudo-pair pipeline; both produce a bare point-estimate change mask/probability. With 6 lakes and no ground truth, this should be wrapped in a bootstrap band across lakes or a conformal-prediction layer (item C7) before it is presented to a panel.
evaluation.augmentation_honesty_risk: High, and this is the note's central concern. Both supervision strategies manufacture training signal synthetically: the weak-temporal-supervision method fabricates 'changed' examples by cross-pairing unrelated locations, and Changen2 generates entire synthetic bi-temporal image/label series with a diffusion model. If either synthetic pipeline is used to manufacture training examples for these specific 6 lakes, and the synthetic changes happen to resemble plausible encroachment patterns (e.g., vegetation-to-built transitions), the resulting model could learn, and then 'detect,' an encroachment signature that is an artefact of the synthetic-data generator's own priors rather than anything observed in the real 2019-2025 imagery. This must be disclosed explicitly wherever a change map derived through synthetic pretraining is shown: it is a qualitative, corroborating product to be checked against independent evidence (desilting records, macrophyte mapping), never presented as a measured or ground-truthed result on its own.

evidence.published_performance: Weak temporal supervision (arXiv 2601.02126), Dual-UNet trained on their extended b-FLAIR aerial data: in-domain b-FLAIR-test F1=79.0%, IoU=65.3% [verify]; out-of-domain zero-shot transfer: LEVIR-CD F1=77.3%/IoU=63.0% [verify], WHU-CD F1=70.6%/IoU=54.5% [verify], S2Looking F1=13.6%/IoU=7.3% [verify] (their own worst transfer result, on the dataset closest in spirit to satellite-based monitoring); low-data regime with 1% of LEVIR-CD training data reaches IoU=0.60 vs 0.36 for a non-pretrained baseline [verify]. Changen2 (arXiv 2406.17998): reported zero-shot change detection narrows the gap to fully-supervised models to about 3% on LEVIR-CD and about 10% on S2Looking and SECOND [verify]; a separately retrieved absolute figure gives LEVIR-CD zero-shot F1 approximately 89.6% (ViT-L), S2Looking approximately 52.7% (ViT-L), SECOND approximately 61.0% (ViT-B) [verify]. All of these figures are v1 preprint / TPAMI-preprint numbers from the authors' own benchmarks, not independently reproduced by this research.
evidence.study_area_of_that_work: Weak-temporal-supervision: France (FLAIR aerial orthophotos, IAILD, SPOT-6/7), 0.2-1.5 m/px. Changen2: globally distributed VHR sites via xView2 (disaster-affected areas worldwide) and OpenEarthMap (global city land cover), sub-2 m/px. Neither study area includes India, wetlands/lakes as a class, or any imagery coarser than 1.5 m/px -- both are far removed in geography, target class and resolution from 6 Bengaluru lakes at 20 m.
evidence.applies_to_indian_urban_lakes: No. No evidence was found of either method, or of generic Siamese/foundation-model change detection generally, being applied to Bengaluru lakes or Indian urban wetlands at Sentinel-2 resolution.
evidence.evidence_recency: 2026 (arXiv 2601.02126, submitted 5 Jan 2026) and 2024 (arXiv 2406.17998 / Changen2, building on the ICCV 2023 Changen predecessor). Both are within the project's required post-2020 window and are current as of the research date (17 Sept 2026).
evidence.primary_sources: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.02126 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2601.02126v1 ; https://xavibou.github.io/CDviaWTS/ ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17998 ; https://arxiv.org/html/2406.17998v1 ; https://github.com/Z-Zheng/pytorch-change-models ; https://github.com/Z-Zheng/Changen ; LEVIR-CD: https://justchenhao.github.io/LEVIR/ ; WHU-CD: DOI 10.1109/TGRS.2018.2858817, https://gpcv.whu.edu.cn/data/building_dataset.html ; S2Looking: DOI 10.3390/rs13245094, https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09244 ; macrophyte cross-check for Bellandur/Varthur: DOI 10.3390/rs12223843.

risk.failure_modes: (1) Resolution mismatch: checkpoints trained to spot multi-pixel buildings at 0.2-1.5 m/px have no equivalent target at 20 m, so applied zero-shot they most likely just re-detect gross spectral change (water-to-vegetation, vegetation-to-bare) rather than anything building-specific; (2) desilting produces a large false-positive 'change' signal indistinguishable from encroachment; (3) hyacinth bloom/die-off produces a second, unrelated source of false-positive change; (4) only 6 lake pairs makes any fine-tuning or threshold calibration unstable and easy to overfit; (5) the 2601.02126 code's public availability is unconfirmed, which could block the weak-temporal-supervision route entirely if the release does not materialise in time.
risk.panel_defensibility: The first question a panel will ask is 'your change detector was built and validated on 0.2-1.5 m imagery of buildings -- how do you know it is measuring anything meaningful over a lake shoreline at 20 m?' There is no honest answer that avoids admitting the resolution gap is unresolved by either 2026 paper; the defensible position is to present the checkpoint's failure or non-transfer as a documented finding, not to quote its LEVIR-CD/S2Looking numbers as evidence of Bengaluru performance. A second predictable question -- 'how do you separate this from desilting or hyacinth?' -- has no automatic answer from either method and requires external cross-checks (D7, the MDPI macrophyte paper) to survive.
risk.honest_expectation: The realistic, reportable outcome is a documented negative/null result: pretrained LEVIR-CD/WHU-CD/S2Looking checkpoints and Changen2's zero-shot mode do not transfer usefully to 20 m Sentinel-2 lake buffers, confirming the resolution-gap trap the project's own note anticipates. A from-scratch, lightweight Siamese network (e.g. FC-Siam-diff, a few hundred thousand parameters) trained directly on the project's own 6-lake Sentinel-2 stack, using MNDWI/NDVI difference as an openly-acknowledged weak proxy label, is more defensible but is then just a differently-shaped implementation of the project's existing classical rule (C5/C8 territory) rather than a genuine deep-learning advance, and should be described that way.

verdict.recommended_rank: reject for direct use of pretrained LEVIR-CD/WHU-CD/S2Looking checkpoints or Changen2 zero-shot as a quantitative model; consider-with-reasons as a documented resolution-gap negative result, or as inspiration for a small from-scratch Siamese network trained on the project's own weak MNDWI/NDVI proxy labels.
verdict.one_line_for_the_guide: We tested pretrained Siamese change-detection checkpoints (LEVIR-CD, WHU-CD, S2Looking) and the Changen2 generative change model and found neither transfers from their 0.2-1.5 m training resolution to our 20 m Sentinel-2 lakes, so we report that resolution-gap trap as a finding rather than presenting their benchmark numbers as evidence for Bengaluru, and instead build any bi-temporal change signal from our own weakly-labelled Sentinel-2 data.
